questions_and_answers.question: After deciding where to go, what formula can you use to discuss the time?
If you agree to the proposed time, what can you say?

answers.answer: Ee, ii desu yo. (Yes, that is fine.)

questions_and_answers.question: What is another way to discuss the time to meet, using 'shimashoo ka'?

answers.answer: (Time) ni shimashoo ka? (Shall we make it (time)?)

questions_and_answers.question: To suggest meeting at 7:00 p.m., which is correct?
What does 'shimashoo' mean and what does 'ni shimashoo ka' mean?

answers.answer: shimashoo = 'let's do'; ni shimashoo ka = 'shall we make it...?'
shimashoo = 'let's go'; ni shimashoo ka = 'shall we eat?'
shimashoo = 'let's see'; ni shimashoo ka = 'where shall we meet?'
shimashoo = 'let's wait'; ni shimashoo ka = 'shall we wait?'

questions_and_answers.question: The expression '...ni shimashoo ka' can propose things other than time. How do you say 'Shall we make it a bar?' and 'Shall we decide on Chinese food?'

answers.answer: Baa ni shimashoo ka? / Chuugoku-ryoori ni shimashoo ka?
Baa de shimashoo ka? / Chuugoku-ryoori de shimashoo ka?
Baa o shimashoo ka? / Chuugoku-ryoori o shimashoo ka?
Baa wa doo desu ka? / Chuugoku-ryoori desu ka?

questions_and_answers.question: When you want to express agreement to a '...ni shimashoo ka' question, what can you say?

articles.text:
3. Deciding the time

After deciding where to go, you will probably talk about the time. You can use this formula:

(Time) wa doo desu ka?    How about (time)?

If you agree to the proposed time, you can say:
Ee, ii desu yo.    Yes, that is fine.

Another way to discuss the time to meet is to use the following expression:
(Time) ni shimashoo ka?    Shall we make it (time)?

For example, if you want to suggest that you meet at 7:00 p.m., you can say:
Shichi-ji ni shimashoo ka?    Shall we make it 7:00 p.m.?

Note again that the particle ni is used after the time expression. The word shimashoo means 'let's do' and shimashoo ka means 'shall we?'

The expression ...ni shimashoo ka 'shall we make it?' is also frequently used to propose things other than time. For example:
Baa ni shimashoo ka?               Shall we make it a bar?
Chuugoku-ryoori ni shimashoo ka?    Shall we decide on Chinese food?

When you want to express agreement to the above questions, you can say:
(Ee), soo shimashoo.    Yes, let's do so.
